purpose: Compare working-game latency and quality on identical tasks; not a live benchmark result.

fixtures.prompt: Create a 20-second game where tapping glowing stars earns points and tapping X-shaped decoys loses points. Support phone touch and keyboard, show score and a replay button.
Create a one-button game where a cat with a jetpack dodges clouds and collects fish. Use procedural art, short rounds, a visible score, and a big replay button. Support touch and Space.
Create an untimed garden toy where tapping grows glowing plants. Include three plant types, a visible collection count, a gentle surprise, and a reset button. Work on phones.
Create a 3-by-3 lights-out puzzle. Guarantee that the starting puzzle is solvable, count moves, detect a win, and offer another puzzle. Support phone and keyboard input.
Create a compact one-button jumping game with three short levels and surprising moving platforms. Include checkpoint restart and a clear win screen. Touch and Space must work.
Create a six-pair memory game with drawn geometric symbols, a move counter, match detection, and restart. Ignore extra clicks while an unmatched pair is being hidden.
Turn the star game into a firefly forest, preserving timer, score, combos, decoys, pause and replay. Draw fireflies and distinguish decoys by shape.
Add a rare golden star worth 50 points. Keep all original mechanics working, and explain the golden star in one short sentence.
Add a visible garden that blooms a new flower every five catches. Keep the game untimed and preserve the finish-round and replay buttons.
Make this a multiplication-only quiz with an easy and hard mode. Keep the timer, feedback, scoring and replay working.
Make the game fit a 320px-wide phone viewport with readable instructions and touch targets at least 44px. Preserve all rules and restart behavior.
Turn this into spotting a tiny alien among friendly robots. Use procedural drawings, preserve all rules, and increase visual difficulty gradually.
